purpose: Per CEO R300 P0+P5: 'Make portfolio accounting explicit. PORTFOLIO_TARGET=15, ACTIVE=14, CEMETERY=1, VACANCY=1. Do not hide vacancy. 15 active slots, no auto-generation, fill from existing only.'
constitutional_basis: Article X (canonical state has one authority). Article XXV (unknown must remain unknown — vacancy is an honest unknown). Article XXVIII (no silent semantic promotion — don't pretend 14=15).

portfolio_accounting.rule: The portfolio target is 15 ACTIVE slots. When a candidate enters the cemetery, a VACANCY is created. The vacancy must be filled from existing WATCH/DISCOVERED/COMMERCIAL_FRAMED candidates — NOT by generating a new invention. This prevents portfolio expansion while maintaining the 15-slot discipline.
portfolio_accounting.anti_inflation_rule: Do NOT report '15 candidates' when one is in the cemetery. Report '14 active + 1 cemetery + 1 vacancy = 15 target slots.' The vacancy is honest.

cemetery.name: Energy-Neutral Micro-Assist (CSF Flow)
cemetery.kill_reason: CSF energy harvesting refuted by EXPERIMENTALLY_MEASURED data (0.62 nW, PubMed 28425028)

vacancy_fill_process.rule: Fill from EXISTING candidates only. No new invention generation. The promoted candidate must pass the portfolio admission gate.
vacancy_fill_process.candidate_search: Search existing WATCH/DISCOVERED/COMMERCIAL_FRAMED candidates from the discovery engine's history (R270-R275 candidate register, cemetery-adjacent WATCH candidates, or any previously identified but not promoted candidate).

modelled_kill_rule_correction.old_rule: MODELLED numbers CANNOT kill a candidate.
modelled_kill_rule_correction.corrected_rule: A modelled result cannot kill a candidate solely because of an unverified assumption that materially determines the result. A modelled result CAN kill when the model is sufficiently validated for the question being asked and the assumptions are independently justified.
modelled_kill_rule_correction.rationale: CEO R300: 'Too absolute. Modelled results can kill when the model is validated and assumptions are justified. Otherwise we risk throwing away useful computational falsification.'
